description: Owner+authority dual-signed authorization for tsukuroi to PROPOSE a defensive fix patch against an authorized target, scoped to an upstream akuma finding. Parallels akuma's scope contract (ADR-2605151400). PROPOSE-ONLY ceiling is structural: mergeAuthorityHeld const false. tsukuroi holds NO platform master key — submission uses an owner-issued least-privilege expiring fork-PR-only credential referenced (not stored) by delegationCredentialRef (ADR-2605231525). R0 = schema skeleton; R1 = additionalProperties=false + required-field enforcement + dual-signature verification.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of mandate emit.

findingCid.description: CID of the upstream akuma finding (or owner-signed finding report) being remediated. G3: the ONLY permitted vulnerability input; tsukuroi performs no probing.

targetRepo.description: Git remote URL (or config target identifier) the patch is proposed to.

allowedPaths.description: Explicit file/dir prefixes tsukuroi MAY touch. G6: pathsTouched ⊆ allowedPaths; writes outside are denied at policy and schema.

submissionMode.description: How the fix is proposed. fork-pr from R2; patch-file from R1; config-diff requires Council Lv7+ at R3.

ownerSignature.description: Detached signature over the mandate payload, verifies against ownerDid. G7.

authoritySignature.description: Detached signature over the same payload, verifies against authorityDid. G7.

legalBasis.description: SOW id / bug-bounty program URL / written-authorization document CID.

delegationCredentialRef.description: REFERENCE (not the secret) to an owner-issued, least-privilege, fork-PR-only, expiring credential stored as ciphertext in vault.etzhayyim.com. G8: tsukuroi never holds a platform-held master/merge credential (ADR-2605231525).

mergeAuthorityHeld.description: G4 PROPOSE-ONLY: structurally false. tsukuroi never holds merge/deploy authority; a human owner merges.

maxPrPerWindow.description: G12 rate limit: max PRs/patches tsukuroi may open per mandate window.

revoked.description: One-way, immediate revocation by either party.
